subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC \u0014 data isolation follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom@finsecure.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finsecure.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC  data isolation follow-up

Tom / Lena  thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few clarifying questions so we can size the right deployment option (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC/on-prem):

- Goal: You mentioned that client data and ML-derived outputs must never traverse shared control planes or be accessible by multitenant services.
- Current understanding: Primary requirement is complete network isolation from other tenants plus customer-managed KMS for keying. Secondary asks: audit logs retention, ability to restrict outbound egress, and SOC 2 evidence.

Questions: 
1) Is it a hard requirement that the control plane itself be customer-managed (i.e., Private deployment) vs. acceptable to have a Redwood-hosted control plane with no customer data stored/shared (Private VPC with isolated compute and customer KMS)?
2) Do you require on-prem (air-gapped) for any workloads, or is VPC-based Private deployment in your cloud account acceptable?
3) Any compliance timelines or existing procurement constraints we should be aware of?

Next steps I propose:
- I can share a short security overview + SOC2 checklist (attached) and a matrix comparing Dedicated vs Private VPC vs Private on-prem.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Neha) to validate network/KMS/egress controls.

If you can ping back answers to the three questions, I'll prepare the appropriate matrix and schedule the follow-up call.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142
[Attachment: redwood_private_vpc_security_overview.pdf]
[Attachment: soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx]

From: Tom Hargreaves <tom@finsecure.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finsecure.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC  data isolation follow-up

Marissa  thanks for the recap and the attachments, helpful. Quick answers below: 

1) Control plane: hard requirement that customer control plane is preferred for our high-risk workloads. We are comfortable with a Private deployment where we own the control plane (private control plane managed in our VPC) OR an on-prem option. Redwood-hosted control plane is a hard no for production PII/PHI workloads. For lower-risk dev/test we can consider hosted.

2) On-prem: Not strictly required for all workloads, but there are two regulated lines of business that require either on-prem or a fully air-gapped deployment. For the rest of the company, Private VPC in AWS (our account) is acceptable as long as there is no route to the public internet from the compute plane and keys are customer-managed (AWS KMS).

3) Timeline / procurement: We are targeting a compliance review by end of Q2 (June). Procurement will require SOC 2 artifacts, encryption details, and a network diagram. We'll likely run a pilot with 1-2 models in April/May.

Can we set up the technical call week of Feb 23? I'd like our infra lead Lena on the call.

Tom Hargreaves
Head of Infrastructure Security | FinSecure
+1 617 555 1225

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hargreaves <tom@finsecure.com>
Cc: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finsecure.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private VPC  data isolation follow-up

Tom  perfect, thanks for the clarifications. Short notes and proposed next steps: 

- Control plane: Understood  we'll treat production PII/PHI workloads as requiring a Private deployment (customer-managed control plane) or an on-prem option. We'll call out dev/test as Hosted-compatible.
- Key management: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations). We'll include key rotation controls and an explanation of our envelope encryption flow in the security brief.
- Network & egress: We'll provide a network diagram that shows compute-only subnets, no NAT gateway by default, and explicit egress-blocking options.
- SOC2 / artifacts: attaching checklist  we'll mark required items for your procurement team.

Next steps: 
1) Technical deep-dive with Neha  suggested slots (all PST): Tue Feb 24 10:00-11:00, Wed Feb 25 14:00-15:00, Thu Feb 26 09:00-10:00. Please let us know which works and we'll send a calendar invite.
2) I'll circulate a deployment comparison matrix (Dedicated vs Private VPC vs Private on-prem) + security brief ahead of the call.

Neha  looping you in to validate the network/KMS/egress controls and to join the technical call.

Thanks  looking forward to the next steps.

Best,
